correctness.rationale: A partial injection is square-zero exactly when domain and image are disjoint. If the hub belongs to the domain and maps to v, at most two other images can be rim neighbors of v, giving rank at most three; inversion handles the image-hub case. The disjointness bound already gives floor(n/2) for even n. For odd n≥7 a larger rank uses the hub but would exceed three. For n=5 a hypothetical rank three has image {v−1,v,v+1}; the two other domain vertices v−2 and v+2 are adjacent, but v−1 and v+1 are not. Two disjoint alternating independent rim sets give the claimed attainable rank, and restriction gives all lower ranks. On the rim, adjacency determines the metric. Red domain and blue image therefore must have identical multisets of path-component orders. For a fixed red composition of k, blue orders contribute r!/∏ m_j!, isomorphisms contribute ∏ m_j!·∏ b_j^(m_j), and b_j is one for singletons and two otherwise. For even n a marked red start has n labels and represents a pair with its map r times, yielding n(r−1)! times the coefficient in B^r. For odd n deleting the unique unused vertex cuts a line, and equal run counts force unlike end colors, yielding 2n r! times that coefficient. With a hub, rank two counts directed rim edges avoiding the other domain vertex (2(n−2) choices); rank three counts the nonedges in the path remaining after deleting v and its neighbors, namely binom(n−3,2)−(n−4), and has two bijections for each. Multiplying by n and by two for inversion gives exactly the listed hub corrections; there are none at rank at least four.
residual_risks: Replay with python3 wheel_squarezero_checker.py directly enumerates disjoint labeled maps for rim sizes 4–12 and larger ranks for 5 and 7; the computations for 13–25 are formula evaluations only. The comment about partitions in the excess-rank checker should be read as a restriction of the direct tests, not a combinatorial restriction on set partitions of larger odd wheels.

broader_coverage.reasoning: W_n for n≥5 is not complete multipartite, as nonadjacency on its rim is not transitive. Counting all maps of a given rank or sorting by induced type does not by itself count isomorphisms of disjoint subsets, which is the joint condition needed here.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Wheel rim maps are induced-subgraph isomorphisms with disjoint sides, but are not generally intrinsic cycle isometries. For instance, on a rim of size six, {1,4} and {2,6} are disjoint and both distance-two pairs in the wheel, but have unequal intrinsic cycle distances.

value.rationale: Square-zero elements expose a genuine difference from the ambient symmetric inverse monoid in odd wheels. The count at the largest attainable rank is a natural semigroup invariant: the parity distinction and hub exceptions give an exact count of the maps with the tightest possible disjointness constraint. The useful contribution is the exact uniform rim/hub enumeration, not the elementary rank upper bound alone.
residual_risks: No full rank distribution, higher-index nilpotency enumeration or larger graph-family generalization is credited.
